+_adv_budget_estimate() {  # <estimated input tokens> <role>=<hop>... → _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL (cents) and _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES (JSON);
+  # each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 output tokens × output rate (micro-USD per Mtok → cents: ÷ 10^10, each term
+  # truncated, as the fixed-rate formula was). An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok and is said;
+  # a zero-priced one estimates 0 and is said too.
+  local tokens="$1"; shift
+  local -a roles=() hops=() args=()
+  local rv rows="" line c_in c_out total=0 voices="[]"
+  for rv in "$@"; do roles+=("${rv%%=*}"); hops+=("${rv#*=}"); args+=(--alias "${rv#*=}"); done
+  if (( ${#hops[@]} > 0 )); then
+    rows=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing \
+      --catalog "${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  fi
+  local k _bv_role _bv_hop _bv_src _bv_in _bv_out _bv_cents
+  for (( k = 0; k < ${#hops[@]}; k++ )); do
+    _bv_role="${roles[$k]}"; _bv_hop="${hops[$k]}"   # (a role word and a validated hop name — the jq operands below are small)
+    line=$(awk -v a="alias=$_bv_hop" '$1 == a { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    if [[ ! "$_bv_in" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || ! "$_bv_out" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || "$_bv_src" == "unknown" || -z "$_bv_src" ]]; then
+      _bv_in=10000000; _bv_out=30000000; _bv_src="fallback"
+      log "budget: no catalog price for $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice"
+    elif (( _bv_in == 0 && _bv_out == 0 )); then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c"
+    elif [[ "$_bv_src" == "stale_catalog" ]]; then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given"
+    fi
+    c_in=$(( tokens * _bv_in / 10000000000 )); c_out=$(( 2000 * _bv_out / 10000000000 )); _bv_cents=$(( c_in + c_out ))
+    total=$(( total + _bv_cents ))
+    voices=$(jq -c --arg r "$_bv_role" --arg h "$_bv_hop" --arg s "$_bv_src" --argjson c "$_bv_cents" --argjson i "$_bv_in" --argjson o "$_bv_out" \
+      '. + [{role: $r, alias: $h, estimated_cents: $c, input_per_mtok: $i, output_per_mtok: $o, pricing_source: $s}]' <<<"$voices")
+  done
+  _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL="$total"; _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="$voices"
+  log "budget: estimate ${total}c over ${#hops[@]} planned voice(s) ($(jq -r 'map("\(.role) \(.alias) \(.estimated_cents)c") | join(", ")' <<<"$voices"))"
+}
+
+# --- advisory voices (D-7.4): after the counted voices, concurrently, one wall clock, findings only under advisory_voices[] ---
+_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""   # "pid=token" pairs of the live advisory walkers (the reapers kill only the process forked)
+_adv_reap_advisory() {
+  local e p
+  for e in ${_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS:-}; do
+    p="${e%%=*}"
+    [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    _adv_is_same "$p" "$e" && { _adv_kill_tree "$p" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_walk() {  # <voice dir> <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias> — one advisory voice: the hop, then
+  # process_findings (the same schema, qualification and KF-004 repair rules as a counted voice); its rejected payloads never
+  # land beside the envelope (verdict-derive counts those), and the result is published whole
+  local d="$1" type="$2" sprint_id="$3" timeout="$4" diff_files="$5" alias="$6" raw="" rc=0 res="" st=""
+  export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REJECT_SIDECAR_DISABLE=1
+  export _ADV_SIDECAR_TAG="advisory"
+  raw=$(_adv_invoke_hop "$alias" "$d/system-prompt.txt" "$d/user-prompt.txt" "$alias" "$timeout" "$d/vq-advisory.json" "$type" "$SCRIPT_DIR/../schemas/wire/dissent-${type}.wire.json") || rc=$?
+  printf '%s' "$rc" > "$d/rc"
+  res=$(process_findings "$raw" "$type" "$alias" "$sprint_id" "$rc" "$diff_files") || res=""
+  if [[ -n "$res" ]]; then st=$(_extract_result_status "$res") || st=""; fi
+  [[ -n "$st" ]] || st="malformed_response"
+  printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/result.json.tmp" && mv -f "$d/result.json.tmp" "$d/result.json"
+  printf '%s' "$st" > "$d/status"
+}
+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.
+  # Each voice's files are under $_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory/<n>/
+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4
+  local root="$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory" n=0 a d pid tok e deadline alive
+  mkdir -p "$root" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+  for a in "$@"; do
+    n=$((n + 1)); d="$root/$n"
+    mkdir -p "$d" 2>/dev/null || continue
+    printf '%s' "$a" > "$d/alias"
+    if cp -f "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/system-prompt.txt" "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/user-prompt.txt" "$d/" 2>/dev/null; then
+      ( _adv_advisory_walk "$d" "$type" "$sprint_id" "$timeout" "$diff_files" "$a" ) >"$d/log" 2>&1 &
+      pid=$!
+      tok=$(_adv_fork_token "$pid") || tok=""
+      _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS+="${pid}=$(_adv_tok_word "$tok") "
+      printf '%s' "$pid" > "$d/pid"
+    else
+      printf 'prompt_copy_failed' > "$d/status"
+    fi
+  done
+  deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT ))
+  while :; do
+    alive=0
+    for e in $_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS; do _adv_is_same "${e%%=*}" "$e" && { alive=1; break; }; done
+    (( alive )) || break
+    (( $(date +%s) < deadline )) || break
+    sleep 0.2
+  done
+  for (( a = 1; a <= n; a++ )); do
+    d="$root/$a"; [[ -s "$d/pid" ]] || continue
+    pid=$(cat "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    for e in $_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS; do
+      [[ "${e%%=*}" == "$pid" ]] || continue
+      if _adv_is_same "$pid" "$e"; then
+        : > "$d/timed_out"
+        _adv_kill_tree "$pid" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+        log "Advisory voice $(cat "$d/alias"): still running at the ${CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT}s advisory wall clock — killed (timed_out)"
+      fi
+      wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+    done
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_block() {  # <type> <counted result json file> <diff file> <alias>…(planned, in order) — the advisory_voices[]
+  # array on stdout: each planned voice's findings (hallucination-filtered, tagged voice: advisory, linked by duplicate_of to a
+  # counted finding with the same file, overlapping lines and the same category) in config order, then every alias locality refused
+  local type="$1" counted="$2" diff_file="$3"; shift 3
+  # (every jq operand below is a small reviewed scalar — a validated alias, a status word, an error cut to 200 characters, a
+  # whole number; the envelopes travel as files)
+  local root="${_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR:-}/advisory" _av_n=0 _av_alias d st res entry _av_rc _av_err
+  mkdir -p "$root" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+  local blk="$root/entries.jsonl"; : > "$blk" || return 1
+  for _av_alias in "$@"; do
+    _av_n=$((_av_n + 1)); d="$root/$_av_n"; st=""; res='{}'; _av_err=""
+    if [[ -e "$d/timed_out" ]]; then st="timed_out"
+    elif [[ -s "$d/result.json" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' "$d/result.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      res=$(cat "$d/result.json")
+      case "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || echo malformed_response)" in
+        malformed_response|api_failure) st="failed"; _av_err=$(jq -r '.metadata.error // .metadata.status // ""' <<<"$res" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177' | cut -c1-200) ;;
+        *) st="succeeded"; res=$(_apply_hallucination_filter "$res" "$diff_file") ;;
+      esac
+    elif [[ "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "prompt_copy_failed" ]]; then st="failed"; _av_err="prompt_copy_failed"
+    else st="failed"; _av_err="the voice left no result"
+    fi
+    _av_rc=$(cat "$d/rc" 2>/dev/null || echo ""); [[ "$_av_rc" =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$ ]] || _av_rc="null"
+    printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/block-in.json"
+    entry=$(jq -c -n --slurpfile cf "$counted" --slurpfile af "$d/block-in.json" --arg a "$_av_alias" --arg st "$st" --arg err "$_av_err" \
+      --argjson rc "$_av_rc" --argjson n "$_av_n" '
+      def anc: (.anchor // "") | if type == "string" then . else "" end;
+      def file: anc | split(":")[0];
+      def lines: ([anc | capture(":(?<a>[0-9]+)(-(?<b>[0-9]+))?$")] | .[0]) as $m
+        | if $m == null then null else ([($m.a | tonumber), (($m.b // $m.a) | tonumber)] | sort) end;
+      def overlaps($x; $y): if $x != null and $y != null then ($x[0] <= $y[1] and $y[0] <= $x[1]) else false end;
+      ($cf[0].findings // []) as $top
+      | ($af[0]) as $r
+      | (if $st == "succeeded" then ($r.findings // []) else [] end) as $fs
+      | {alias: $a, status: $st, counted_as: "advisory_voice",
+         findings: ($fs | to_entries | map(.value as $f
+           | ($f | file) as $ff | ($f | lines) as $fl | ($f | anc) as $fa
+           | ($top | map(select((file) == $ff and $ff != "" and ((.category // "") == ($f.category // ""))
+                                and (if (lines) != null and $fl != null then overlaps(lines; $fl) else (anc) == $fa end)))
+                   | (.[0].id // null)) as $dup
+           | $f + {id: ("DISS-A" + ($n | tostring) + "-" + ((.key + 1) | tostring | if length < 3 then ("000" + .)[-3:] else . end)),
+                   voice: "advisory", answered_by: $a, duplicate_of: $dup})),
+         rejected_count: ($r.metadata.rejected_count // 0), repaired_count: ($r.metadata.repaired_count // 0),
+         rejected_summary: ($r.metadata.rejected_summary // []),
+         cost_usd: ($r.metadata.cost_usd // 0), exit_code: $rc}
+        + (if $err == "" then {} else {error: $err} end)' 2>/dev/null) \
+      || entry=$(jq -cn --arg a "$_av_alias" '{alias: $a, status: "failed", counted_as: "advisory_voice", findings: [], error: "the advisory block could not be built"}')
+    printf '%s\n' "$entry" >> "$blk"
+    log "Advisory voice $_av_alias: $st ($(jq -r '.findings | length' <<<"$entry") finding(s), never counted)"
+  done
+  # the aliases refused by locality, named in the block too (never run)
+  local r_role _av_alias_r _av_prov_r
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_role _av_alias_r _av_prov_r; do
+    [[ "$r_role" == "advisory" && -n "$_av_alias_r" ]] || continue
+    jq -cn --arg a "$_av_alias_r" --arg p "$_av_prov_r" '{alias: $a, status: "refused", counted_as: "advisory_voice", findings: [],
+      error: ("locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop " + $a + " (" + $p + ")")}' >> "$blk"
+  done <<<"$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED"
+  jq -cs '.' "$blk"
+}

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

1	"""Per-provider endpoint policy on the cheval Python path (cycle-129 FR-7, SDD D-7.2, D-8.0).
2	
3	The rule, applied at config load to every HTTP provider in the merged ``hounfour.providers`` view:
4	
5	* ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` is a host STRING, never a boolean. It must be an IP literal or ``localhost``
6	  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
7	  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
8	  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
9	* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
10	  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
11	* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
12	  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
13	  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
14	* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
15	  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
16	  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.
17	
18	ONE implementation: every URL and opt-in decision here is made by the canonical
19	``.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py`` (the module the bash callers and the health probe use),
20	loaded by path as ``loa_cheval.codegen.emit_endpoint_validator_ts`` does: ``check_insecure_optin`` for the
21	opt-in and ``validate_declared_endpoint`` (the full pipeline minus the host allowlist, which an
22	operator-declared https host is not on) for the endpoint. The refusal codes are therefore the validator's
23	codes, and URL parsing stays confined to that module (the cycle-099 import guard).
24	``tests/test_endpoint_validator_optin.py`` runs one case table through both entry points.
25	
26	Request-time half (``TransportPolicy`` in ``providers/base.py``): for an opted-in provider, or a model whose
27	``dispatch_group`` is ``local``, the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects and
28	requires every request URL to stay under the declared endpoint path.
29	
30	CLI (used by ``model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>``; reads the merged config, never prints a secret)::
31	
32	    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy list-providers [--project-root DIR]
33	    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy describe-provider NAME [--project-root DIR]
34	"""
35	
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import argparse
39	import importlib.util
40	import json
41	import re
42	import sys
43	import threading
44	from pathlib import Path
45	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
46	
47	from loa_cheval.types import ConfigError
48	
49	# The literal auth values normalised to keyless (D-8.0). Only "local": any other literal could be a real key.
50	KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS = frozenset({"local"})
51	
52	# .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py → .claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py
53	_VALIDATOR_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "lib" / "endpoint-validator.py"
54	_VALIDATOR: Any = None
55	_VALIDATOR_LOCK = threading.Lock()
56	
57	
58	def _validator() -> Any:
59	    """The canonical endpoint-validator module, loaded once by path. A missing
60	    or unloadable validator is a ConfigError (fail-closed: no endpoint is
61	    admitted unchecked)."""
62	    global _VALIDATOR
63	    with _VALIDATOR_LOCK:
64	        if _VALIDATOR is not None:
65	            return _VALIDATOR
66	        name = "loa_endpoint_validator_canonical"
67	        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, _VALIDATOR_PATH)
68	        if spec is None or spec.loader is None or not _VALIDATOR_PATH.is_file():
69	            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} not found; reinstall the framework")
70	        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
71	        sys.modules[name] = module
72	        try:
73	            spec.loader.exec_module(module)
74	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any load failure is fail-closed
75	            sys.modules.pop(name, None)
76	            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} failed to load: {exc}") from exc
77	        _VALIDATOR = module
78	        return module
79	
80	
81	class EndpointPolicyError(ConfigError):
82	    """A provider endpoint or opt-in refused at load. ``policy_code`` is the endpoint-validator code."""
83	
84	    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str, provider: Optional[str] = None):
85	        where = f"providers.{provider}: " if provider else ""
86	        super().__init__(f"[{code}] {where}{detail}", context={"policy_code": code, "provider": provider})
87	        self.policy_code = code
88	        self.detail = detail
89	
90	
91	def split_url(url: str) -> Tuple[str, str, Optional[int], str]:
92	    """(scheme, canonical host, explicit port or None, path) via the canonical validator; ValueError on a bad URL."""
93	    return _validator().split_url(url)
94	
95	
96	def canonical_optin_host(value: Any, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
97	    """Validate an ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` value and return its canonical host, or raise."""
98	    ok, code, detail, host = _validator().check_insecure_optin(value)
99	    if not ok:
100	        raise EndpointPolicyError(code or "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-INVALID", detail or "invalid opt-in", provider)
101	    return host
102	
103	
104	def check_endpoint(endpoint: str, allow_insecure_endpoint: Any = None, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
105	    """Apply the D-7.2 rule to one provider's endpoint. Returns the canonical opt-in host (or None); raises."""
106	    optin = canonical_optin_host(allow_insecure_endpoint, provider) if allow_insecure_endpoint is not None else None
107	    result = _validator().validate_declared_endpoint(endpoint, allow_insecure_endpoint=optin)
108	    if not result.valid:
109	        raise EndpointPolicyError(result.code or "ENDPOINT-INVALID", result.detail or "endpoint refused", provider)
110	    return optin
111	
112	
113	# --- the merged view --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	
115	
116	def _is_cli_provider(prov: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
117	    ptype = str(prov.get("type") or "")
118	    if ptype.endswith("-headless"):
119	        return True
120	    models = prov.get("models") or {}
121	    return bool(models) and isinstance(models, dict) and all(
122	        isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("kind") == "cli" for m in models.values()
123	    )
124	
125	
126	def normalise_keyless(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
127	    """Pre-interpolation step: a literal ``auth: "local"`` becomes ``keyless: true`` (D-8.0); ``keyless`` must be a bool."""
128	    providers = merged.get("providers")
129	    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
130	        return
131	    for name, prov in providers.items():
132	        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
133	            continue
134	        if "keyless" in prov and not isinstance(prov["keyless"], bool):
135	            raise ConfigError(
136	                f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.keyless must be true or false, got {prov['keyless']!r}"
137	            )
138	        auth = prov.get("auth")
139	        if isinstance(auth, str) and auth.strip().lower() in KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS:
140	            prov["keyless"] = True
141	
142	
143	def validate_providers(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
144	    """Post-interpolation step: endpoint rule and keyless preconditions for every provider."""
145	    providers = merged.get("providers")
146	    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
147	        return
148	    for name, prov in providers.items():
149	        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
150	            continue
151	        optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
152	        endpoint = prov.get("endpoint")
153	        if not _is_cli_provider(prov) and endpoint not in (None, ""):
154	            if not isinstance(endpoint, str):
155	                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.endpoint must be a string")
156	            check_endpoint(endpoint, optin, name)
157	        elif optin is not None:
158	            # An opt-in with nothing to apply to is still validated, so a typo never sits silent.
159	            canonical_optin_host(optin, name)
160	        if prov.get("keyless") is True:
161	            models = prov.get("models") or {}
162	            if not isinstance(models, dict) or not models:
163	                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name} is keyless but declares no models")
164	            for model_id, model in models.items():
165	                model = model if isinstance(model, dict) else {}
166	                cw = model.get("context_window")
167	                if not isinstance(cw, int) or isinstance(cw, bool) or cw <= 0:
168	                    raise ConfigError(
169	                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
170	                        f"with a declared context_window (a positive integer)"
171	                    )
172	                if not model.get("dispatch_group"):
173	                    raise ConfigError(
174	                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
175	                        f"with a declared dispatch_group"
176	                    )
177	
178	
179	# --- probe helper CLI -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
180	
181	_ENV_AUTH = re.compile(r"^\{env:([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}$")
182	
183	
184	def describe_provider(merged: Dict[str, Any], name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
185	    """What the health probe needs about one configured provider. Never carries a secret value."""
186	    prov = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(name)
187	    if not isinstance(prov, dict):
188	        raise KeyError(name)
189	    raw_auth = getattr(prov.get("auth"), "_raw", prov.get("auth"))
190	    auth_env = None
191	    if isinstance(raw_auth, str):
192	        m = _ENV_AUTH.match(raw_auth.strip())
193	        if m:
194	            auth_env = m.group(1)
195	    optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
196	    models = prov.get("models") or {}
197	    return {
198	        "name": name,
199	        "type": prov.get("type", "openai"),
200	        "endpoint": prov.get("endpoint") or "",
201	        "keyless": prov.get("keyless") is True,
202	        "allow_insecure_endpoint": canonical_optin_host(optin, name) if optin is not None else None,
203	        "auth_env": auth_env,
204	        "cli": _is_cli_provider(prov),
205	        "models": sorted(models.keys()) if isinstance(models, dict) else [],
206	    }
207	
208	
209	def _main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
210	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="endpoint_policy")
211	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
212	    lp = sub.add_parser("list-providers")
213	    lp.add_argument("--project-root", default=None)
214	    dp = sub.add_parser("describe-provider")
215	    dp.add_argument("name")
216	    dp.add_argument("--project-root", default=None)
217	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
218	
219	    from loa_cheval.config.loader import load_config
220	
221	    try:
222	        merged, _sources = load_config(project_root=args.project_root)
223	    except ConfigError as exc:
224	        print(json.dumps({"error": "config_load_failed", "detail": str(exc)}), file=sys.stderr)
225	        return 78
226	    if args.cmd == "list-providers":
227	        print("\n".join(sorted((merged.get("providers") or {}).keys())))
228	        return 0
229	    try:
230	        print(json.dumps(describe_provider(merged, args.name), sort_keys=True))
231	    except KeyError:
232	        print(json.dumps({"error": "provider_not_configured", "provider": args.name}), file=sys.stderr)
233	        return 64
234	    return 0
235	
236	
237	if __name__ == "__main__":
238	    raise SystemExit(_main())
239

+++ b/.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py
@@ -50,7 +50,10 @@ from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
 
-import idna  # ≥ 3.6, RFC 5891

 EXIT_VALID = 0
 EXIT_REJECTED = 78  # EX_CONFIG (sysexits.h)
@@ -936,6 +939,11 @@ def _idna_normalize(host: str) -> str:
         host = host[:-1]
     if all(ord(c) < 128 for c in host) and "xn--" not in host.lower():
         return host.lower()
+    try:
+        import idna
+    except ImportError as exc:
+        # Caller maps UnicodeError to ENDPOINT-IDN-NOT-ALLOWED (fail-closed).
+        raise UnicodeError(f"idna is not installed; an IDN host cannot be validated ({exc})") from None
     try:
         encoded = idna.encode(host, uts46=False, transitional=False).decode("ascii")
         return encoded.lower()
@@ -984,10 +992,114 @@ def _provider_for_host(
     return None, None
 
 
-def validate(url: str, allowlist: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]) -> ValidationResult:
+# =============================================================================
+# cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.2): per-provider insecure-endpoint opt-in.
+#
+# `allow_insecure_endpoint` is a host STRING naming one loopback or RFC1918 host
+# as an IP literal or `localhost` (never resolved, so no DNS rebinding). With it,
+# a URL whose host equals the opt-in host is admitted over http or https on any
+# port (the host allowlist and the loopback/private IP block do not apply to that
+# one host); an http URL to any other host is ENDPOINT-INSECURE-HOST-MISMATCH; an
+# https URL to any other host runs the unchanged pipeline. The opt-in is passed
+# per call, so one provider's opt-in never reaches another provider's URL.
+#
+# Twin: .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py (the cheval Python
+# path). The refusal codes are the same strings; the cheval test
+# tests/test_endpoint_validator_optin.py runs one case table through both.
+# =============================================================================
+
+_OPTIN_LOOPBACK = (ipaddress.ip_network("127.0.0.0/8"), ipaddress.ip_network("::1/128"))
+_OPTIN_RFC1918 = (
+    ipaddress.ip_network("10.0.0.0/8"),
+    ipaddress.ip_network("172.16.0.0/12"),
+    ipaddress.ip_network("192.168.0.0/16"),
+)
+_OPTIN_METADATA = frozenset({"169.254.169.254", "fd00:ec2::254"})
+_OPTIN_ULA_V6 = ipaddress.ip_network("fc00::/7")
+
+
+def _canonical_host(host: str) -> str:
+    h = str(host).strip().lower()
+    if h.startswith("[") and h.endswith("]"):
+        h = h[1:-1]
+    if h.endswith(".") and not h.endswith(".."):
+        h = h[:-1]
+    try:
+        return str(ipaddress.ip_address(h))
+    except ValueError:
+        return h
+
+
+def check_insecure_optin(value: Any) -> tuple[bool, str | None, str | None, str | None]:
+    """Validate an `allow_insecure_endpoint` value. Returns (ok, code, detail, canonical_host)."""
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-BOOLEAN",
+                f"allow_insecure_endpoint must be a host string (an IP literal or localhost), "
+                f"not the boolean {value!r}", None)
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
+        return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-INVALID",
+                f"allow_insecure_endpoint must be a non-empty host string, got {value!r}", None)
+    raw = value.strip()
+    if any(c in raw for c in ("\r", "\n", "\t", "\x00")) or "/" in raw or "@" in raw:
+        return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-INVALID",
+                f"allow_insecure_endpoint {raw!r} must be a bare host (no scheme, path, port or userinfo)", None)
+    host = _canonical_host(raw)
+    if host == "localhost":
+        return True, None, None, host
+    try:
+        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(host)
+    except ValueError:
+        return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-DNS-NAME",
+                f"allow_insecure_endpoint {raw!r} is a DNS name; only an IP literal or localhost is admitted "
+                "(an insecure endpoint is never resolved, so it cannot be rebound)", None)
+    if str(addr) in _OPTIN_METADATA:
+        return False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-METADATA", f"allow_insecure_endpoint {raw!r} is a cloud metadata address", None
+    if addr.is_link_local:
+        return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-LINK-LOCAL",
+                f"allow_insecure_endpoint {raw!r} is link-local (169.254/16, fe80::/10)", None)
+    if any(addr in net for net in _OPTIN_LOOPBACK + _OPTIN_RFC1918 if addr.version == net.version):
+        return True, None, None, str(addr)
+    if addr.version == 6 and addr in _OPTIN_ULA_V6:
+        return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-NOT-LOCAL",
+                f"allow_insecure_endpoint {raw!r} is a unique-local IPv6 address; only loopback or RFC1918 is admitted",
+                None)
+    return (False, "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-NOT-LOCAL",
+            f"allow_insecure_endpoint {raw!r} is not a loopback or RFC1918 address", None)
+
+
+def split_url(url: str) -> tuple[str, str, int | None, str]:
+    """(lower-cased scheme, canonical host, explicit port or None, path) of a URL.
+    The host is lower-cased, unbracketed and, for an IP literal, in compressed
+    form. Raises ValueError on a URL that does not parse (bad port included).
+    The cheval Python path uses this so URL parsing stays in this module."""
+    parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
+    port = parts.port  # raises ValueError for a non-integer or out-of-range port
+    return parts.scheme.lower(), _canonical_host(parts.hostname or ""), port, parts.path or ""
+
+
+def validate_declared_endpoint(url: str, *, allow_insecure_endpoint: Any = None) -> ValidationResult:
+    """cycle-129 D-7.2: the pipeline for an endpoint the OPERATOR declared in the
+    merged hounfour config (the cheval Python path). Every step runs except the
+    step-8 host/port allowlist — an operator-declared https host (Azure, a hosted
+    open-weight API) is the operator's choice — and, because that backstop is

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).

    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...

One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:

    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>

A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
    that exists;
  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.

This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

MAX_DEPTH = 10


def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
        out = dict(base)
        for key, value in overlay.items():
            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
        return out
    return overlay


def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    import yaml

    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
    if config_path:
        try:
            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
        except FileNotFoundError:
            project = {}
        if not isinstance(project, dict):
            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
    return merged


def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
        if isinstance(target, dict):
            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
            return target.strip()
    return None


def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
    name = (hop or "").strip()
    if not name:
        return None
    current, seen = name, set()
    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
        if ":" in current:
            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
        if not target:
            break
        if target in seen:
            return None
        seen.add(current)
        current = target
    if ":" in current:
        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None


def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
    seen = set(_seen or ())
    target = resolve(hop, merged)
    if target is None:
        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
    provider, model = target
    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
    if not isinstance(block, dict):
        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
    if group != "local":
        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
    if key in seen:
        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
    seen.add(key)
    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
    if not isinstance(chain, list):
        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
    for nxt in chain:
        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
        p2, loc, _ = classify(nxt, merged, _depth + 1, seen)
        if loc != "local":
            return provider, "hosted", f"fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:{nxt}({p2})"
    return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"


def _clean(text: str) -> str:
    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in "\t" else "_" for c in text)[:128]


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--config", default="")
    ap.add_argument("hops", nargs="*")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        merged = load_merged(args.catalog, args.config or None)
        err = ""
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed: every hop hosted, the reason said once
        merged, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}"
        print(f"hop-locality: the merged config could not be read ({err}) — every hop is hosted", file=sys.stderr)
    for hop in args.hops:
        if merged is None:
            print(f"{_clean(hop)}\tunknown\thosted\tconfig_unreadable")
            continue
        provider, loc, reason = classify(hop, merged)
        print(f"{_clean(hop)}\t{_clean(provider)}\t{loc}\t{_clean(reason)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

is_flatline_enabled() {
    local enabled
    enabled=$(read_config '.flatline_protocol.enabled' 'false')
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]]
}

get_model_primary() {
    read_config '.flatline_protocol.models.primary' 'opus'
}

get_model_secondary() {
    read_config '.flatline_protocol.models.secondary' 'gpt-5.3-codex'
}

# Provisional resolution — will be replaced by Hounfour router capability
# query when ModelPort interface is available (see loa-finn #31).
# The function signature is the durable contract; the config lookup is temporary.
#
# Checks hounfour config first (canonical), then flatline_protocol.models.tertiary (alias)
# Returns empty string when not configured (2-model mode preserved)
# Cache avoids repeated yq invocations during a single Flatline run
_CACHED_TERTIARY_MODEL=""
_CACHED_TERTIARY_MODEL_SET=false

# cycle-127 FR-1: a tertiary routed to agy (the gemini-headless hop) with hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in not true
# is NOT PLANNED — get_model_tertiary returns empty (2-model mode) and the status reads disabled_by_opt_in.
get_model_tertiary() {
    if [[ "$_CACHED_TERTIARY_MODEL_SET" == true ]]; then
        echo "$_CACHED_TERTIARY_MODEL"
        return
    fi
    local model
    model=$(_get_model_tertiary_configured)
    if [[ -n "$model" ]] && _tertiary_routes_to_agy "$model" && ! _agy_opted_in; then
        model=""
    fi
    _CACHED_TERTIARY_MODEL="$model"
    _CACHED_TERTIARY_MODEL_SET=true
    echo "$model"
}

_get_model_tertiary_configured() {  # the configured tertiary, before the agy opt-in gate
    local model
    model=$(read_config '.hounfour.flatline_tertiary_model' '')
    if [[ -z "$model" ]]; then
        model=$(read_config '.flatline_protocol.models.tertiary' '')
    fi
    echo "$model"
}

_agy_opted_in() {  # true only for a YAML boolean true at hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in (lib/agy-gate-lib.sh; no env override)
    agy_opted_in "$CONFIG_FILE"
}

_tertiary_routes_to_agy() {  # <model> → 0 when cheval would dispatch it through agy (lib/agy-gate-lib.sh routes_to_agy:
    # the gemini-headless hop by name, or a Google model under hounfour.headless.mode cli-only — env wins, as cheval's)
    routes_to_agy "$1" "$(agy_headless_mode "$CONFIG_FILE")" "$CONFIG_FILE"   # (r251-4: project aliases resolved first)
}

tertiary_opt_in_skip_reason() {  # prints the skip line and returns 0 when the configured tertiary is gated off
    local m
    m=$(_get_model_tertiary_configured)
    [[ -n "$m" ]] && _tertiary_routes_to_agy "$m" && ! _agy_opted_in || return 1
    echo "Tertiary model '$m' not planned: disabled by opt-in (the agy route needs hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true) — 2-model Flatline, not a degraded voice"
}

get_tertiary_status() {  # active | disabled | disabled_by_opt_in
    if [[ -n "$(get_model_tertiary)" ]]; then echo "active"
    elif tertiary_opt_in_skip_reason >/dev/null; then echo "disabled_by_opt_in"
    else echo "disabled"; fi
}

# cycle-116 D3 (bd-c116-d3-tiering): per-stage tier routing opt-in.
# advisor_strategy.stage_routing.flatline_scorer (default false) governs
# whether score-mode cross-scoring dispatch is routed through the
# advisor_strategy role/skill resolver (cheval.py:1069 role gate) instead
# of the hardcoded --model pin. Default false => byte-identical to today.
# Nested map leaves room for future per-stage keys without a schema churn.
# Cached to avoid a per-score-call yq invocation.
_CACHED_STAGE_ROUTING_SCORER=""
_CACHED_STAGE_ROUTING_SCORER_SET=false
is_stage_routing_scorer_enabled() {
    if [[ "$_CACHED_STAGE_ROUTING_SCORER_SET" == true ]]; then
        [[ "$_CACHED_STAGE_ROUTING_SCORER" == "true" ]]
        return
    fi
    local v
    v=$(read_config '.advisor_strategy.stage_routing.flatline_scorer' 'false')
    _CACHED_STAGE_ROUTING_SCORER="$v"
    _CACHED_STAGE_ROUTING_SCORER_SET=true
    [[ "$v" == "true" ]]
}

get_max_iterations() {
    read_config '.flatline_protocol.max_iterations' '5'
}

    local failures=0
    for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do

    if [[ $success_count -lt 2 ]]; then

+    ignored, an HTTP redirect is an error and is never followed, and every request
+    URL must keep the declared endpoint's scheme, host and port and start with its
+    path. The load-time half lives in config/endpoint_policy.py."""

# gemini-3.2-pro, claude-fable-6) can set them in config and the
# pattern admits them; provider-side validation at API call time catches
# typos/invalid names with a clearer error than a pre-runtime allowlist.
# Note: gemini pattern requires X.Y (with dot). Variants like gemini-3-flash
# don't match and must wait for explicit allowlist addition.
VALID_MODEL_PATTERNS=(
    '^gpt-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-codex|-pro)?$'     # openai: gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.3-codex
    '^claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku|fable)-[0-9]+([-.][0-9]+)?$'  # anthropic: claude-opus-5, claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5
    '^gemini-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-flash|-pro)?(-preview)?$'  # google: gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3.1-pro-preview (cycle-109 T3.4 #793: -preview suffix)
    '^(opus|sonnet|haiku|fable)$'            # short anthropic aliases (DISS-002: anchored alternation)
    # cycle-109 Sprint 3 T3.4 (#793): cheval-headless pin form.
    # PR #727 (cycle-098) introduced subscription-auth headless adapters;
    # the orchestrator's pre-validator must admit the canonical pin shape
    # so operators following the cycle-098/099 setup don't fall back to
    # API providers (which defeats the cost-via-subscription benefit).
    '^(claude|codex|gemini)-headless:.+$'    # cheval-headless pin form
)

# Read declarations only: validation must not dispatch or resolve credentials.
# Reuse the loader's merge and the routing resolver's alias semantics.
# python3 -I (sprint-250 audit LOW-003): no cwd entry on sys.path, so a json.py or yaml.py in the cwd is never
# imported; -I also discards PYTHONPATH, so the adapters directory arrives as argv[1] and is inserted below
configured_flatline_model() {
    python3 -I - "$SCRIPT_DIR/../adapters" "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$1" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from loa_cheval.config.loader import load_system_defaults, load_project_config, _deep_merge
from loa_cheval.routing.resolver import resolve_alias

try:
    config = _deep_merge(load_system_defaults(sys.argv[2]), load_project_config(sys.argv[2]))
    providers = config.get("providers", {})
    aliases = {**config.get("backward_compat_aliases", {}), **config.get("aliases", {})}
    model = sys.argv[3]
    if ":" not in model and model not in aliases:
        matches = [name for name, provider in providers.items() if model in provider.get("models", {})]
        if not matches:
            sys.exit(1)
        if len(matches) != 1:
            sys.exit(2)
        print(f"{matches[0]}:{model}")
    else:
        resolved = resolve_alias(model, aliases)
        if resolved.provider not in providers:
            sys.exit(2 if model in aliases else 1)
        if resolved.model_id not in providers[resolved.provider].get("models", {}):
            sys.exit(2)
        print(f"{resolved.provider}:{resolved.model_id}")
except Exception:
    sys.exit(2)
PY
}

validate_model() {
    local model="$1"
    local config_key="$2"  # e.g., "primary" or "secondary"

    if [[ -z "$model" ]]; then
        error "Flatline model '$config_key' is empty. Set flatline_protocol.models.$config_key in .loa.config.yaml"
        error "Valid models: ${VALID_FLATLINE_MODELS[*]}"
        return 1
    fi

    # Project declarations take precedence over generated defaults, including
    # aliases that override a known name. A declared but broken target fails.
    if declare -F configured_flatline_model >/dev/null; then
        local configured_rc=0
        configured_flatline_model "$model" >/dev/null || configured_rc=$?
        case "$configured_rc" in
            0) return 0 ;;
            2) error "Invalid or ambiguous configured Flatline model: '$model'"; return 1 ;;
        esac
    fi

    # Explicit allowlist match
    for valid_model in "${VALID_FLATLINE_MODELS[@]}"; do
        if [[ "$model" == "$valid_model" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    # Forward-compat pattern match — accept plausible model names so operators
    # running new vendor releases don't need to wait for a Loa update. The
    # provider-side call will reject actually-invalid names with a clearer
    # error than a pre-runtime allowlist.
    for pattern in "${VALID_MODEL_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        if [[ "$model" =~ $pattern ]]; then
            log "Flatline model '$model' (config_key=$config_key) accepted via forward-compat pattern" >&2
            return 0
        fi
    done

    error "Unknown flatline model: '$model' (from flatline_protocol.models.$config_key in .loa.config.yaml)"
    error "Known-good models: ${VALID_FLATLINE_MODELS[*]}"
    error "Forward-compat patterns also accepted: gpt-X.Y(-codex|-pro), claude-{opus|sonnet|haiku|fable}-X(-Y), gemini-X.Y(-flash|-pro)"
    error "Note: '$model' may be an agent alias, not a model name. Check .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml for alias mappings."
    return 1

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.5, SDD D-7.4, D-7.6).
#
# The dissent budget pre-check prices every planned voice — the primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory voice —
# at its catalog price (python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias), instead of the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok.
# An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 for that voice and is said by name; a zero-priced entry estimates
# zero and is said too. Prices come from fixture entries in the test's project config (hounfour.providers overlays the
# catalog, as cheval merges it). Each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 × output rate, micro-USD/Mtok → cents.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bud; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

_cfg() {  # <model> <budget> <companion_voice> [extra code_review lines]
    s3_config "hounfour:
  providers:
    openai:
      models:
        fixture-priced:
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 2000000, output_per_mtok: 8000000}
    fixturelocal:
      models:
        fixture-zero:
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        fixture-stale:
          price_date: \"2000-01-01\"
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 1000000, output_per_mtok: 1000000}
flatline_protocol:
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    model: $1
    budget_cents: $2
    timeout_seconds: 30
    companion_voice: $3
    fallback_chain: []
${4:-}"
}

_big_diff() {  # a diff whose estimate is 1,000,500 input tokens (3,000,000 bytes / 3 + 500)
    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( 3000000 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch")" -eq 3000000 ]
}

@test "BUD-1 the primary is priced at its catalog rate (no fixed-rate fallback): 1,000,500 tokens × 2 + 2000 × 8 USD/Mtok = 201c" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg fixture-priced 150 false
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "201" ]
    [ "$(jq -c '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | {role, alias, estimated_cents, pricing_source}]' <<<"$result")" = '[{"role":"primary","alias":"fixture-priced","estimated_cents":201,"pricing_source":"config"}]' ]
    grep -qF "budget: estimate 201c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-priced 201c)" "$T/stderr.log"
    ! grep -q "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "a catalog-priced primary fell back"; return 1; }
    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
}

@test "BUD-2 an alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok for that voice, said by name (1000c + 6c)" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg mystery-model-x 150 false
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.estimate_voices[0].pricing_source' <<<"$result")" = "fallback" ]
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (primary) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice" "$T/stderr.log"
    [ "$(grep -c "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log")" = "1" ]
}

@test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse" {
    _cfg fixture-zero 0 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (primary) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qF "budget: estimate 0c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-zero 0c)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qx "fixture-zero" "$CALLS"
    # the same run priced at the fixed rate is refused (the regression this replaces: 2000 output tokens × 30 = 6c > 0)
    _cfg mystery-model-x 0 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
}

@test "BUD-4 the gate sums every planned voice: primary + the companion's first hop + each advisory voice" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg fixture-priced 1 true "    advisory_voices: [fixture-zero, mystery-model-x]"
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | "\(.role)=\(.alias)"] | join(" ")' <<<"$result")" = "primary=fixture-priced companion=claude-headless advisory=fixture-zero advisory=mystery-model-x" ]
    # the companion's price is the catalog's (whatever it is today): recompute it from the same CLI
    local row ci co comp
    row=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias claude-headless --config "$CONFIG_FILE")
    ci=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row"); co=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row")
    [[ "$ci" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$co" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
    comp=$(( 1000500 * ci / 10000000000 + 2000 * co / 10000000000 ))
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[1].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$comp" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[2].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "0" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[3].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$(( 201 + comp + 0 + 1006 ))" ]
    [ "$(jq '[.metadata.estimate_voices[].estimated_cents] | add' <<<"$result")" = "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" ]
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (advisory) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (advisory)" "$T/stderr.log"
}

@test "BUD-5 a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) is used as given and said" {
    _cfg fixture-stale 1000 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-stale (primary) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given" "$T/stderr.log"
}

@test "BUD-6 with no price CLI answer at all every voice falls back and is said (the gate never prices from nothing)" {
    _cfg fixture-priced 1000 false
    # a PYTHONPATH that cannot import the package: the CLI fails, every planned voice is unknown
    local real patched
    real="$(declare -f _adv_budget_estimate)"
    patched="${real/PYTHONPATH=\"\$PROJECT_ROOT\/.claude\/adapters\"/PYTHONPATH=/nonexistent}"
    [ "$patched" != "$real" ]   # (the seam was found: the CLI really cannot be imported in this run)
    eval "$patched"
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for fixture-priced (primary)" "$T/stderr.log"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/adversarial-review-locality.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.5 (PRD FR-8 AC-8.1 … AC-8.3, SDD D-8.0 … D-8.2,
# DEC-0146).
#
# Under hounfour.locality: local_voices, adversarial-review.sh plans only hops whose provider has dispatch_group: local in
# the merged config (catalog + the project's hounfour.providers) and refuses every hosted hop of its inventory at plan time
# by name — primary chain, companion chain, advisory voices, the KF-004 repair chain (tiny, claude-headless, any pin; the
# chain is the answering voice). With one local family the audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW, the gate and verdict-derive
# treat the envelope as today, and the output says so. The default (hosted) is unchanged. Mock mode: the harness stub.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3loc; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

# one hosted provider (openai, the catalog's) and one local provider (localbox, declared here)
_cfg() {  # <locality value | absent> [extra code_review / security_audit lines]
    local loc=""; [[ "$1" == absent ]] || loc="  locality: $1"
    s3_config "hounfour:
$loc
  providers:
    localbox:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: \"http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1\"
      models:
        qwen-local:
          dispatch_group: local
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        qwen-local-b:
          dispatch_group: local
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        qwen-local-c:
          dispatch_group: local
        qwen-leaky:
          dispatch_group: local
          fallback_chain: [\"openai:gpt-5.5\"]
  aliases:
    lq: \"localbox:qwen-local\"
    lqb: \"localbox:qwen-local-b\"
    lqc: \"localbox:qwen-local-c\"
flatline_protocol:
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    model: gpt-5.5
    budget_cents: 500
    timeout_seconds: 30
    fallback_chain: [lq]
${2:-}
  security_audit:
    enabled: true
    model: gpt-5.5
    budget_cents: 500
    timeout_seconds: 30
    fallback_chain: [lq]
${3:-}"
}

_hosted_in() {  # <file of hop names, one per line> → the hosted ones, as hop-locality.py classifies them against this config
    local hops; hops=$(sed 's/^repair://' "$1" | sort -u | grep -v '^$' || true)
    [[ -n "$hops" ]] || return 0
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" \
        --config "$CONFIG_FILE" -- $hops | awk -F'\t' '$3 != "local" { print $1 }'
}

@test "LOC-1 one hosted and one local provider: only the local hop is planned and every hosted hop is refused by name" {
    _cfg local_voices
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
    # the dispatched hops: the local one only
    [ "$(sort -u "$CALLS" | tr '\n' ' ')" = "lq " ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.final_model' "$env")" = "lq" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.model_attempts | join(",")' "$env")" = "lq:reviewed" ]
    # each refusal named: the hosted primary, the companion's default hop, the repair chain's two hosted hops
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop gpt-5.5 (openai)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop claude-headless (anthropic)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop tiny (anthropic)" "$T/stderr.log"
    # the companion was not planned: its chain had no local hop — never rerouted
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.planned' "$env")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.reason' "$env")" = "locality_refused" ]
    # the envelope names the posture and each refusal with its role
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.locality.mode' "$env")" = "local_voices" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.locality.refused[] | "\(.role):\(.alias):\(.provider)"] | sort | join(" ")' "$env")" = \
      "companion:claude-headless:anthropic primary:gpt-5.5:openai repair:claude-headless:anthropic repair:tiny:anthropic" ]
    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "1" ]
}

@test "LOC-3 redaction-style: in a whole run with a rejected payload, an Anthropic key and the CLIs present, no hosted alias is ever dispatched" {
    _cfg local_voices "    advisory_voices: [lqc, gpt-5.5-pro]
    companion_chain:
      anthropic: [opus, lqb]"
    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="fixture-not-a-key" OPENAI_API_KEY="fixture-not-a-key"

# --- /v1/chat/completions streaming parser ---


def parse_openai_chat_stream(
    byte_iter: Iterator[bytes],
    *,
    provider: str = "openai",
    model_data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    reasoning_class: bool = False,
    now_provider: Any = time.monotonic,
) -> CompletionResult:
    """Parse OpenAI /v1/chat/completions SSE stream.

    Chunk shape (one per `data:` line):
        {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"Hello"},
          "finish_reason":null}],"model":"...","usage":null}

    Terminator: `data: [DONE]`

    Tool-call assembly: each `delta.tool_calls[i]` may carry partial
    fragments — `function.name` appears once on the first delta, then
    `function.arguments` arrives as concatenated chunks across subsequent
    deltas. Index-keyed accumulator handles parallel tool calls.

    Usage: final chunk may contain `usage: {...}` (per OpenAI's
    `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` request body — most LLM SDKs
    request this by default for cost accounting).

    cycle-113 sprint-169 T2.2: kwargs `model_data`, `reasoning_class`,
    `now_provider` wire the StreamingRecoveryTracker per SDD §3.3.
    Tool-call `function.arguments` deltas are NOT fed to the tracker
    (tool-only responses legitimately empty-content; feeding would
    confuse the empty_content_window detector). Raises
    ``StreamingRecoveryAbort`` per FR-B-2 / I-2.
    """
    # cycle-113 T2.2 — recovery tracker init (parity with anthropic T1.6).
    recovery_config = StreamingRecoveryConfig.for_model(
        model_data or {}, reasoning_class=reasoning_class,
    )
    recovery_tracker = StreamingRecoveryTracker(
        config=recovery_config,
        start_time_s=now_provider(),
    )
    config_applied: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "first_token_deadline_s": recovery_config.first_token_deadline_s,
        "empty_content_window_tokens": recovery_config.empty_content_window_tokens,
        "cot_budget_tokens": recovery_config.cot_budget_tokens,
        "reasoning_class": recovery_config.reasoning_class,
    }
    partial_text_seen: List[str] = []

    text_parts: List[str] = []
    # cycle-129 FR-7 (D-7.3): reasoning trace deltas — progress, never content.
    reasoning_parts: List[str] = []
    # tool_calls accumulator keyed by index. Each entry:
    #   {"id": str, "name": str, "arguments_parts": [str, ...]}
    tool_calls_by_index: Dict[int, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    finish_reason: Optional[str] = None
    final_model: Optional[str] = None
    usage_data: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    for chunk in _iter_chat_stream_chunks_with_deadline(
        byte_iter, recovery_tracker, config_applied, now_provider,
    ):
        if chunk is None or chunk == "[DONE]":
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(chunk)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            # Sprint 4A cycle-3 (BF-006): fail-closed on malformed data frames.
            # Under uncertainty about whether the stream is intact, halt rather
            # than forward partial — mirrors the cycle-098 fail-closed pattern.
            # Keep-alive lines (`:`-prefixed comments) never reach this branch
            # because the SSE parser strips them upstream; only legitimate
            # `data:` payloads land here, and a malformed payload almost always
            # indicates protocol corruption or truncation.
            raise ValueError(
                f"OpenAI streaming malformed data frame: {chunk[:200]!r}"
            )

        # Sprint 4A cycle-3 (BF-002): top-level `{"error":...}` frame detection.
        # Without this, an OpenAI error frame (no `choices` array) would be
        # silently skipped by the `if not choices: continue` arm below, and
        # the parser would return an empty CompletionResult flagged as
        # successful — the cycle-102 ghost manifesting one layer wider in
        # the very substrate built to surface it. Fail-loud invariant.
        if isinstance(payload.get("error"), dict):
            err = payload["error"]
            raise ValueError(
                f"OpenAI streaming error frame: type={err.get('type')!r} "
                f"code={err.get('code')!r} message={err.get('message')!r}"
            )

        final_model = payload.get("model") or final_model

        # OpenAI's stream_options.include_usage path attaches usage on the
        # final chunk with an empty `choices` array.
        if payload.get("usage"):
            usage_data = payload["usage"]

        choices = payload.get("choices") or []
        if not choices:
            continue
        choice = choices[0] or {}
        if choice.get("finish_reason"):
            finish_reason = choice["finish_reason"]

        delta = choice.get("delta") or {}

        # cycle-129 FR-7 (D-7.3): a local reasoning model streams its trace as
        # `delta.reasoning_content` before any content. It keeps the recovery
        # tracker alive (first-token deadline) but is never fed to the content
        # state machine and never reaches `content`; it lands in `thinking`.
        for _rkey in REASONING_DELTA_KEYS:
            _rtext = delta.get(_rkey)
            if isinstance(_rtext, str) and _rtext:
                recovery_tracker.on_progress(now_provider())
                accumulate_capped(
                    reasoning_parts, _rtext, cap=MAX_TEXT_PART_BYTES, kind="reasoning"
                )

        # Text content
        content = delta.get("content")
        if content is not None:
            # cycle-113 T2.2: feed tracker on content deltas (incl. empty
            # strings per SDD §2.1). Refusal text is also visible content
            # and gets the same treatment below.
            _recovery_feed_openai(
                recovery_tracker, content, partial_text_seen,
                config_applied, now_provider,
            )
            if content:
                accumulate_capped(
                    text_parts, content, cap=MAX_TEXT_PART_BYTES, kind="text"
                )

        # Refusal (Responses API style; rare on /chat/completions but possible)
        refusal = delta.get("refusal")
        if refusal is not None:
            _recovery_feed_openai(
                recovery_tracker, refusal, partial_text_seen,

"""cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.3; sprint-257 Task 3.2, AC-3.2) — thinking traces from local
reasoning models on the OpenAI paths.

* Streamed `delta.reasoning_content` deltas count as progress for the recovery tracker
  (they satisfy the first-token deadline) and never reach `content`; they land in
  `thinking`.
* Leading `<think>…</think>` blocks and an unterminated leading `<think>` are stripped
  from the content before qualification on the streaming and the non-streaming path;
  `thinking_stripped` is recorded in the result metadata (cheval copies it to MODELINV).
* The model's `streaming_recovery` block reaches the stream parser.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from loa_cheval.providers import openai_adapter as oa  # noqa: E402
from loa_cheval.providers.openai_adapter import OpenAIAdapter  # noqa: E402
from loa_cheval.providers.openai_streaming import parse_openai_chat_stream, strip_thinking_blocks  # noqa: E402
from loa_cheval.streaming import StreamingRecoveryAbort  # noqa: E402
from loa_cheval.types import CompletionRequest, ModelConfig, ProviderConfig  # noqa: E402


def _sse(*payloads: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[bytes]:
    return [f"data: {json.dumps(p)}\n\n".encode() for p in payloads] + [b"data: [DONE]\n\n"]


def _delta(**delta: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"choices": [{"delta": delta, "finish_reason": None}], "model": "m"}


class _Clock:
    """Advances `step` seconds on every read — each SSE event costs `step` seconds."""

    def __init__(self, step: float):
        self.t = 0.0
        self.step = step

    def __call__(self) -> float:
        self.t += self.step
        return self.t


SLOW = {"streaming_recovery": {"first_token_deadline_s": 5}}


def test_reasoning_deltas_keep_the_tracker_alive_and_never_reach_content():
    chunks = _sse(
        _delta(reasoning_content="Let me look at the diff. "),
        _delta(reasoning_content="The loop is off by one. "),
        _delta(reasoning_content="So the finding is the bound."),
        _delta(content='{"findings": []}'),
        {"choices": [{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "model": "m"},
    )
    # every event costs 3 s against a 5 s first-token deadline: content arrives at ~15 s
    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", model_data=SLOW, now_provider=_Clock(3.0))
    assert result.content == '{"findings": []}'
    assert "off by one" in (result.thinking or "")
    assert "Let me look" not in result.content
    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is True
    assert result.metadata["streaming_recovery"]["config_applied"]["first_token_deadline_s"] == 5.0


def test_control_without_reasoning_progress_the_deadline_fires():
    chunks = _sse(
        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},     # keep-alive-shaped frames: no content, no reasoning
        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},
        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},
        _delta(content='{"findings": []}'),
    )
    with pytest.raises(StreamingRecoveryAbort) as info:
        parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", model_data=SLOW, now_provider=_Clock(3.0))
    assert info.value.reason == "first_token_deadline"


def test_reasoning_alias_key_and_no_empty_content_abort():
    # 300 reasoning deltas exceed the 200-token empty-content window if they were fed as content
    many = [_delta(reasoning="step ") for _ in range(300)]
    chunks = _sse(*many, _delta(content="answer"))
    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", now_provider=_Clock(0.001))
    assert result.content == "answer"
    assert result.thinking.startswith("step step")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("raw, content, removed, stripped", [
    ("<think>plan</think>\n{\"a\": 1}", '{"a": 1}', "plan", True),
    ("  <THINK>one</THINK><think>two</think> answer", "answer", "one\ntwo", True),
    ("<think>never closed, the budget ran out", "", "never closed, the budget ran out", True),
    ('{"note": "the template uses <think> tags"}', '{"note": "the template uses <think> tags"}', "", False),
    ("answer first <think>late</think>", "answer first <think>late</think>", "", False),
    ("", "", "", False),
], ids=["block", "two-blocks-case", "unterminated", "inside-answer-kept", "not-leading-kept", "empty"])
def test_strip_thinking_blocks(raw, content, removed, stripped):
    assert strip_thinking_blocks(raw) == (content, removed, stripped)


def test_think_block_stripped_on_the_streaming_path():
    chunks = _sse(_delta(content="<think>reasoning "), _delta(content="here</think>\n"),
                  _delta(content='{"findings": [1]}'))
    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", now_provider=_Clock(0.01))
    assert result.content == '{"findings": [1]}'
    assert result.thinking == "reasoning here"
    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is True


def test_hosted_shaped_stream_records_thinking_stripped_false():
    chunks = _sse(_delta(content='{"findings": []}'))
    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="openai", now_provider=_Clock(0.01))
    assert result.content == '{"findings": []}'
    assert result.thinking is None
    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is False


# --- through the adapter -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _adapter(**model_kwargs: Any) -> OpenAIAdapter:
    return OpenAIAdapter(ProviderConfig(
        name="local", type="openai_compat", endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", auth="", keyless=True,
        allow_insecure_endpoint="127.0.0.1",
        models={"m": ModelConfig(capabilities=["chat"], context_window=32768, endpoint_family="chat",
                                 dispatch_group="local", **model_kwargs)},

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/adversarial-review-advisory.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.3, SDD D-7.4, DEC-0165, DEC-0155).
#
# Advisory voices run after the counted voices on the same prompts, concurrently, under one wall clock; their findings
# live ONLY under advisory_voices[].findings (voice: advisory, counted_as: advisory_voice, duplicate_of links); the rest of
# the envelope and the verdict-derive output are byte-identical (normalised: timestamps removed) with and without them;
# a failed or timed-out advisory voice is a status, never a verdict input; an attempt to count one is refused by name.
# Mock mode: invoke_dissenter is the harness stub (tests/unit/adversarial-review-s3-helpers.bash) — no model is called.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3adv; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

_base_cfg() {  # [extra lines for the code_review block]
    s3_config "flatline_protocol:
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    model: gpt-5.5-pro
    budget_cents: 500
    timeout_seconds: 30
    fallback_chain: []
${1:-}"
}

_feedback() {  # an approved review next to the envelope, for verdict-derive
    mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
    printf '%s\n' 'All good' '' 'No issues found.' \
      '<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-x","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->' \
      > "$OUT_DIR/engineer-feedback.md"
}

_vd() {  # → verdict-derive's --json output on the standing envelope (status recorded, output kept whatever it is)
    "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$OUT_DIR/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>"$T/vd.err" || true
}

@test "ADV-1 an advisory voice's findings are present only under advisory_voices[].findings, tagged and linked by duplicate_of" {
    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two]"
    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
    # the counted voices are untouched: primary + companion, nothing advisory at the top level
    [ "$(jq '.findings | length' "$env")" = "2" ]
    [ "$(jq '[.findings[] | select(.voice == "advisory")] | length' "$env")" = "0" ]
    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
    # the block
    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' "$env")" = "1" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].alias' "$env")" = "adv-two" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].status' "$env")" = "succeeded" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].counted_as' "$env")" = "advisory_voice" ]
    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices[0].findings | length' "$env")" = "3" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[0].findings[].voice] | unique | join(",")' "$env")" = "advisory" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[0].findings[].id] | join(",")' "$env")" = "DISS-A1-001,DISS-A1-002,DISS-A1-003" ]
    # same file, overlapping lines (9-12 over 10), same category → the counted primary finding; else null
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "DISS-001" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[1].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "null" ]   # (line 40: no overlap)
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[2].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "null" ]   # (same line, another category)
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].answered_by' "$env")" = "adv-two" ]
    grep -qx "adv-two" "$CALLS"
    # stdout carries the same envelope
    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' <<<"$result")" = "1" ]
}

@test "ADV-2 the envelope without advisory_voices and the verdict-derive --json output are byte-identical with and without advisory voices" {
    _feedback
    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two; BEHAVIOUR[adv-reject]=reject; BEHAVIOUR[adv-fail]=fail
    _base_cfg
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    cp "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" "$T/without.json"
    _vd > "$T/vd-without.json"
    ls "$OUT_DIR" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$T/ls-without"
    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two, adv-reject, adv-fail]"
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    cp "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" "$T/with.json"
    _vd > "$T/vd-with.json"
    ls "$OUT_DIR" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$T/ls-with"
    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' "$T/with.json")" = "3" ]
    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$T/without.json" >/dev/null
    # the normalised envelopes (advisory_voices deleted, timestamps removed, keys sorted) are byte-identical
    diff <(s3_norm "$T/without.json") <(s3_norm "$T/with.json")
    # …and each named input on its own, so a failure names it
    local k
    for k in '.findings' '.verdict_quality' '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' '.verdict_quality.voices_succeeded' \
             '.metadata.companion_voice' '.metadata.rejected_summary' '.metadata.rejected_sidecars' '.metadata.cost_usd'; do
        [ "$(jq -cS "$k" "$T/without.json")" = "$(jq -cS "$k" "$T/with.json")" ] || { echo "differs: $k"; return 1; }
    done
    # verdict-derive reads the same envelope and sidecars: its --json output is byte-identical
    [ -s "$T/vd-without.json" ]
    diff "$T/vd-without.json" "$T/vd-with.json"
    # the advisory voice's rejected payload never landed beside the envelope (verdict-derive would count it)
    diff "$T/ls-without" "$T/ls-with"
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[] | select(.alias == "adv-reject") | .rejected_count' "$T/with.json")" = "1" ]
}

@test "ADV-3 a failed or malformed advisory voice is recorded under advisory_voices[].status and ignored by verdict quality" {
    BEHAVIOUR[adv-fail]=fail; BEHAVIOUR[adv-bad]=malformed
    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-fail, adv-bad]"
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[].status] | join(",")' "$env")" = "failed,failed" ]
